waveStateWithoutNativeEvent: There is no native 'wave exhausted' or 'wave cleared' event: Mastermind keeps a List<Mastermind.MastermindEvent> m_events and SurvivalWave carries m_state (eSurvivalWaveState) plus m_populationPointsSpentTotal / m_populationPointsSpentDuringWave / m_populationPointsPerWaveMax. Exhaustion has to be derived (state Done, or spent >= per-wave max), and clearing has to be derived from Mastermind.m_activeGroups / m_events becoming empty.

There is no native 'spawn shortfall' event. The only inputs are the requested population spend versus the actual EnemyGroup spawn results (Mastermind.SpawnGroup returns void, so the count must be observed through group registration).

There is no native 'encounter paused' event. The closest native state is SurvivalWave.eSurvivalWaveState.InitialPause (1) and WaitForGroupSpawn (3) inside the wave's own timer machine; a Forge pause would have to hold the wave or stop and re-spawn it.
EnemySpawner, SurvivalWaveGroup and SurvivalWaveSettingsSupplier are empty shells in this build (every method resolves to the shared thunk at RVA 0x353190), so they cannot carry any of these events.

hooks.name: OnSpawn
hooks.entry: replicator spawn callback of the wave object; calls Mastermind.AddEvent (verified direct edge)
hooks.reads: the whole pSurvivalWaveSpawnData: eventID, settingsID, populationDataID, populationPointsSpentTotal/DuringWave, WaveState, courseNode, spawnType, spawnDelay, areaDistance
hooks.harmony: prefix; this is the single point where a wave becomes live and where the EventID needed for the handle is available

hooks.name: OnDespawn
hooks.entry: replicator despawn callback; calls Mastermind.RemoveEvent (verified direct edge)
hooks.harmony: prefix; fires for every teardown, including level cleanup, so a cleared trigger must also check that the encounter was not cancelled

hooks.name: StopEvent
hooks.entry: Mastermind.MastermindEvent.StopEvent override; calls Mastermind.RemoveEvent (verified direct edge)
hooks.harmony: prefix; this is the native per-wave stop entry the Mastermind uses when it tears an event down from the objective or puzzle side

hooks.name: MastermindUpdate
hooks.entry: Mastermind.MastermindEvent per-tick pump; drives the wave state machine
hooks.harmony: postfix per-tick readback; it is the only periodic hook that sees the wave state machine, and it also shows InitialPause/WaitForGroupSpawn for a pause-like trigger

hooks.name: SpawnGroup
hooks.entry: private per-group spawn step; calls SurvivalWave.GetScoredSpawnPoint and SurvivalWave.TriggerDirRandomization (verified direct edges); the EnemyGroup is created outside this body, so group creation has to be observed through Mastermind.RegisterGroup
hooks.reads: m_settings (SurvivalWaveSettingsDataBlock population points), m_populationPointsSpentDuringWave, m_courseNode, m_spawnDirection
hooks.harmony: prefix/postfix per batch; this is the per-batch spawn point that wave_spawned should be derived from

hooks.name: TryEndEvent
hooks.entry: private wave completion test used by the wave's own update
hooks.reads: returns whether the wave considers itself finished
hooks.harmony: postfix on the returned bool; the closest native signal to 'this wave is done spawning and has nothing left to spend'

hooks.name: RegisterCost
hooks.entry: private budget bookkeeping called when a group is paid for
hooks.reads: the float population cost of one group; adds into m_populationPointsSpentTotal/DuringWave
hooks.harmony: prefix records the requested cost; comparing the sum of requested costs with the groups actually registered is the only native basis for a shortfall trigger

hooks.name: RegisterGroup
hooks.entry: private group registration called after a group was produced
hooks.reads: the EnemyGroup and the isRecall flag; calls SurvivalWave.TryPlayWaveDialogSound (verified direct edge)
hooks.harmony: postfix counts the groups that actually registered; paired with WaveRegisterCost it gives requested-versus-delivered

hooks.name: DeSpawn
hooks.entry: wave-side despawn request (the native counterpart of a stop action)
hooks.harmony: prefix; a Forge wave_stop should call this or StopEvent rather than removing the event list entry itself

hooks.name: AddEvent
hooks.entry: master event registry; only caller is SurvivalWave.OnSpawn (verified direct edge)
hooks.harmony: prefix; the authoritative 'a wave event now exists' point, independent of the wave object's own state

hooks.name: RemoveEvent
hooks.entry: master event registry removal; callers are SurvivalWave.StopEvent and SurvivalWave.OnDespawn (verified direct edges)
hooks.harmony: postfix; combined with Mastermind.m_events/m_activeGroups emptiness this is the cleared signal

hooks.name: UnregisterGroup
hooks.harmony: postfix; when the last group of an encounter unregisters the encounter is cleared

catalogMismatches: encounter/wave/spawn_shortfall and the encounter/wave actions belong to ForgeEnemy, while this evidence file lives in ForgeMap/evidence; the file must be moved or mirrored when the ForgeEnemy evidence set is created.

The catalog models an 'encounter' as a native object with start/pause/stop; the game has no encounter type. The nearest native owners are Mastermind (event list plus active groups), SurvivalWave (one event) and the door's ActiveEnemyWaveData.

forge.trigger.encounter.encounter_paused and forge.action.map.encounter_pause have no native counterpart at all: the only pause-like states are internal wave timers (InitialPause, WaitForGroupSpawn) and the door suppression flag.
forge.trigger.encounter.spawn_shortfall has no native event; the game only exposes requested cost and registered groups, so Forge must define the condition.
forge.trigger.encounter.wave_exhausted has no native event either; eSurvivalWaveState.Done and the population-point fields are the only inputs.

GenericEnemyWaveData.TriggerAlarm exists inside every objective wave entry, so the catalog's split between encounter triggers and alarm triggers is not a native distinction: an objective wave can itself start an alarm.
unproven: Every side/host claim is inference from the call graph and Master naming; the Mastermind singleton was not observed at runtime.

The mapping from one wave to its batches is not directly readable: m_isNewWave, m_waveSpawnTimer, m_groupSpawnTimer and RegisterCost calls are the inputs, but the batch boundary must be reconstructed.
SurvivalWave.m_populationPointsSpentDuringWave versus m_populationPointsPerWaveMax semantics (per wave versus per group) are field names only; the exact comparison that ends a wave was not decoded.
GetScoredSpawnPoint returns a spawn point but Mastermind.SpawnGroup returns void, so a native spawn failure cannot be observed without counting registered groups.
Whether Mastermind.MastermindEvent.StopEvent is called for every teardown path, or whether some paths only call SurvivalWave.OnDespawn, is not established.
Door active enemy waves (ActiveEnemyWaveData) were not traced to a concrete spawn call; SetActiveEnemyWaveEnabled only flips a flag.
GroupSpawner, EnemySpawner, SurvivalWaveGroup and SurvivalWaveSettingsSupplier are empty in this build, so any older documentation that hooks them does not apply to build 20403457.
inGameVerificationPlan: Start an objective wave and log SurvivalWave.OnSpawn, SpawnGroup, RegisterCost, RegisterGroup, TryEndEvent, Mastermind.AddEvent/RemoveEvent, RegisterGroup/UnregisterGroup and m_state per tick on host and client; this fixes the batch boundary and the exhaustion condition.
Kill all spawned enemies before the wave budget is spent and observe whether wave_cleared can be distinguished from wave_exhausted (m_activeGroups empty while m_events still holds the wave).
Force a spawn point shortage (small room, blocked spawn points) and log the requested cost versus registered groups to calibrate the shortfall threshold.
Trigger a door active enemy wave and check whether anything beyond SetActiveEnemyWaveEnabled runs, and on which peer.
Confirm the client side sees OnSpawn/OnDespawn but not MastermindUpdate/SpawnGroup, which decides which triggers are host-only.
